senators.name: John Cornyn
senators.note: Lost the Republican primary runoff to Ken Paxton on 2026-05-26; his term ends 2027-01-03.

cards.name: Ken Paxton
facts: Born in Minot, North Dakota, where his father was stationed with the U.S. Air Force.
Served as student body president at Baylor University.
Ran his own law firm in McKinney, Texas, for 14 years before entering public office.
positions: Says he will help complete the border wall, secure the border and deport people who are in the country illegally.
Supports cutting taxes and federal spending, citing the national debt, and removing regulations on energy companies.
Says he will take on large pharmaceutical and food companies and seek more transparency in the food and health care systems.
Says he will protect gun rights and "defend the unborn".

cards.name: James Talarico
cards.role: Member, Texas House of Representatives, District 50 (in the House since 2018)
facts: Taught sixth-grade language arts at Rhodes Middle School on the West Side of San Antonio.
Worked as a nonprofit director before serving in the Texas House.
Describes himself as a Presbyterian seminarian.
positions: Supports comprehensive immigration reform, more Border Patrol agents and a path to citizenship for long-term residents, spouses and DREAMers.
Says he will cut taxes for working people, cap credit card interest rates and have billionaires and large corporations pay more.
Supports letting Americans of any age join Medicare and capping out-of-pocket prescription drug costs.
Supports banning super PACs and corporate PACs and banning stock trading by members of Congress.

senators.name: Dan Sullivan
senators.note: Holds the seat on the 2026 ballot; seeking a third term. Sworn in Jan. 6, 2015; reelected 2020.

senators.name: Lisa Murkowski
senators.note: Appointed Dec. 20, 2002; elected 2004, 2010, 2016 and 2022. Seat not up in 2026.

cards.name: Dan S. Sullivan
facts: Born in Fairview Park, Ohio; has lived in Alaska for 29 years, in Fairbanks and Anchorage.
Was sworn in as Alaska's eighth U.S. senator on Jan. 6, 2015, and was reelected in 2020.
Married to Julie Fate Sullivan since 1994; they have three daughters.
positions: Says he has expanded Alaska energy production from the NPR-A and ANWR to lower costs and create jobs.
Says he passed laws to reduce bycatch, clean up oceans and ban imports of Russian and Chinese trawl-caught fish.
Supports the 2025 tax and spending law he voted for, which he says ends taxes on tips and raises the child tax credit to $2,200.
Says he has delivered a military and Coast Guard buildup in Alaska, including a $7 billion recapitalization of Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson and four icebreakers.

cards.name: Mary Peltola
cards.role: Former U.S. Representative for Alaska's at-large district (2022-2025)
facts: Born in Anchorage; grew up in Kwethluk, Tuntutuliak, Platinum and Bethel along the Kuskokwim River, and has lived in Anchorage since 2025.
Became the first Alaska Native sworn into Congress in September 2022, succeeding the late Rep. Don Young.
Has seven children; two of her sons have served in the U.S. Coast Guard.
positions: Supports federal permitting reform for Alaska energy projects and backs the Alaska LNG pipeline.
Supports banning factory trawling and reducing bycatch to restore Alaska fisheries.
Supports ending federal income tax for Alaskans earning under $92,000 a year, paid for by higher taxes on millionaires and billionaires.
Supports 12-year term limits for members of Congress and a ban on congressional stock trading.

snapshot.rcv_note: Votos de primera preferencia. El conteo por orden de preferencia será el 18 de noviembre; siguen llegando votos por correo.

senators.name: Roger Marshall
senators.note: Seat up in 2026; Marshall is the Republican nominee.

senators.name: Jerry Moran
senators.note: Class 3 seat; term runs to 2029-01-03. First elected to the Senate in 2010 (term began 2011-01-03; sworn in 2011-01-05).

cards.name: Roger Marshall
facts: Practiced as an OB-GYN in Great Bend for 25 years; his campaign says he delivered more than 5,000 babies.
Served as chairman of the board of Great Bend Regional Hospital for 14 years.
Grew up in a fifth-generation Kansas farm family and was the first in his family to attend college.
positions: Supports removing countervailing duties on imported phosphate fertilizer to lower farm input costs; lead sponsor of S. 4418, the Lowering Input Costs for American Farmers Act.
Supports 24- and 72-hour decision deadlines for Medicare Advantage prior-authorization requests; lead sponsor of S. 1816, the Improving Seniors' Timely Access to Care Act.
Supports building a southern border wall; cosponsor of S. 42, the Build the Wall Act, and of the Laken Riley Act (S. 5), signed into law in January 2025.
Supports year-round sales of E15 fuel; cosponsor of S. 593, the Nationwide Consumer and Fuel Retailer Choice Act.

cards.name: Adam Hamilton
cards.role: Senior pastor, United Methodist Church of the Resurrection, Leawood, Kansas (founding pastor, since 1990)
facts: Started the Church of the Resurrection in the Kansas City area in 1990 with his wife, LaVon, beginning with four people.
Has written more than 30 books.
Is a fifth-generation Kansan whose family settled in Dickinson County, according to his campaign.
positions: Supports requiring congressional approval before new tariffs take effect.
Supports expanding Medicare drug-price negotiation and restoring the Affordable Care Act premium subsidies.
Supports prohibiting members of Congress and their households from buying or selling individual stocks while in office.
Supports passing a full farm bill and year-round sales of E15 fuel.

senators.name: Susan Collins
senators.note: Seat up in 2026; seeking a sixth term. Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee.

senators.name: Angus King
senators.note: Independent; caucuses with Senate Democrats. Former Governor of Maine (two terms). Seat not up in 2026.

cards.name: Susan Collins
cards.role: U.S. Senator from Maine (since 1997); Chair, Senate Appropriations Committee
facts: Grew up in Caribou, where her family runs a lumber business founded in 1844; both of her parents served as mayor of Caribou.
Began her career on the staff of Maine Rep. and later Sen. William Cohen after graduating from college in 1975.
Was first elected to the Senate in 1996 and re-elected in 2002, 2008, 2014 and 2020; is seeking a sixth term in 2026.
positions: Says she authored the Social Security Fairness Act, signed into law in 2025, and that it restored earned benefits for more than 25,000 Mainers.
Supports making Medicare telehealth flexibilities permanent and says she has worked to increase federal funding for Alzheimer's and diabetes research.
Supports expanding access to workforce training and says she authored the Paycheck Protection Program for small businesses during the pandemic.
Says she has used her role as Appropriations Committee chair to direct federal funding to projects in all 16 Maine counties.

cards.name: Troy Jackson
cards.role: Former President of the Maine Senate (2018-2024)
facts: Grew up in Allagash and worked as a logger, the fifth generation of his family to work in the woods.
Says he entered politics after helping lead a 1998 loggers' blockade at the Maine-Canada border over the hiring of Canadian workers.
Was nominated by a Maine Democratic Party convention in Bangor on July 25, 2026, replacing the June primary winner, who withdrew on July 10.
positions: Supports Medicare for All and federal negotiation of prescription drug prices; says he would cosponsor the Medicare for All Act.
Supports higher taxes on billionaires and large corporations, lifting the Social Security payroll-tax cap, and expanding the Child Tax Credit and Earned Income Tax Credit.
Supports abolishing U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and an immigration system focused on due process and public-safety threats.
Supports passing a federal law establishing a right to abortion.

senators.name: Jon Husted
senators.note: Appointed by Gov. Mike DeWine to the seat JD Vance vacated; the 2026 special election decides who holds it until 2029-01-03.

cards.name: Jon Husted
cards.role: U.S. senator from Ohio (appointed; in office since January 2025)
facts: Spent his first months in foster care before being adopted by Jim and Judy Husted.
Played defensive back on the University of Dayton team that won the 1989 NCAA Division III football national championship.
As lieutenant governor, directed the Governor's Office of Workforce Transformation and led the InnovateOhio initiative.
positions: Supports pressing state utility regulators to require data centers to pay their own utility costs; sponsored the Senate Ratepayer Protection Act (S.5028).
Supports letting states align eligibility rules across public-assistance programs so that earning more does not cut benefits abruptly (his Upward Mobility Act).
Supports requiring voters to show photo identification in federal elections; sponsored S.5271 to amend the Help America Vote Act.
Says he has worked in the Senate to secure the border and to give law enforcement more tools against fentanyl trafficking.

cards.name: Sherrod Brown
cards.role: Former U.S. senator from Ohio (2007-2025); most recent office
facts: Chaired the Senate Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs from 2021 to 2025.
Founded the Dignity of Work Institute, a nonprofit think tank focused on workers, in March 2025.
Is married to Connie Schultz, a Pulitzer Prize-winning columnist and author.
positions: Opposes trade deals that he says hurt Ohio workers.
Supports capping the cost of insulin and lowering prescription drug prices for seniors.
Opposes tax breaks for corporations and billionaires that he says come at the expense of Ohio workers.
Supports protecting workers' pensions and Social Security benefits, citing his work restoring full Social Security payments to public-sector retirees.

senators.name: Gary Peters
senators.note: Announced on 2025-01-28 that he would not seek a third term; his term ends 2027-01-03. Term began 2015-01-03; sworn in 2015-01-06.

cards.name: Abdul El-Sayed
cards.role: Former director, Wayne County Department of Health, Human and Veterans Services (most recent office, 2023-2025)
facts: Was hired in 2015 to lead Detroit's Health Department after the city's bankruptcy and held the post until 2017.
Was a Rhodes Scholar at the University of Oxford and later taught public health at Columbia University.
Was a candidate in Michigan's 2018 Democratic primary for governor.
positions: Supports Medicare for All, covering every American with no premiums, copays or deductibles, including vision, dental and hearing care.
Supports banning large corporations that speculate on the housing market from owning homes.
Supports overturning the Citizens United decision and banning outside spending by super PACs and corporate 501(c)(4) groups.
Supports a tax on wealth over $1 billion and a higher marginal tax rate on earnings over $1 million.

cards.name: Mike Rogers
cards.role: Former U.S. Representative for Michigan's 8th District (most recent office, 2001-2015); business owner working in cybersecurity since 2015
facts: Worked as an FBI special agent in Chicago on organized crime and public corruption cases before entering politics.
Chaired the House Intelligence Committee and served on the House Energy and Commerce Committee during his time in Congress.
Was the Republican nominee for U.S. Senate in Michigan in 2024.
positions: Supports fining hospitals and insurers that do not publicly post real prices, and penalties for insurers with excessive claim denials or delays.
Supports expanding 529 savings plans to cover first-time home down payments and making new home construction tax-free in designated residential zones.
Says he will work to bring manufacturing jobs back to the United States.
Says he will protect Social Security and Medicare for seniors.
